overview.text: Alien is a 1979 science-fiction horror film directed by Ridley Scott and written by Dan O’Bannon. Its story follows the crew of the commercial spaceship Nostromo, who investigate a mysterious signal and encounter alien life. When a creature gets aboard, the crew must try to survive in the isolated ship. Sigourney Weaver plays officer Ellen Ripley. The film stands out for its claustrophobic spaceship setting, its largely unseen threat, and the unsettling creature designs of artist H.R. Giger. The British Film Institute calls it Scott’s breakthrough sci-fi horror, and the American Film Institute records that it won the 1979 Academy Award for visual effects.

key_facts.text: The film was released on May 25, 1979; Ridley Scott directed it, and Dan O’Bannon wrote it.
The Nostromo is a commercial ship carrying ore; its crew investigates a signal and finds alien life.
Sigourney Weaver plays Ripley, one of the Nostromo crew members.
H.R. Giger helped shape the alien’s design; the BFI highlights the film’s visual and conceptual design as a defining feature.
The film won the 1979 Academy Award for Best Visual Effects and is rated R.
